cnvs: an HTML canvas graphics device

Source: R/cnvs-package.R
cnvs-package.Rd

cnvs implements a small, heavily commented R graphics device that writes plots out as a self-contained HTML file: a <canvas> element plus a <script> block containing the JavaScript CanvasRenderingContext2D calls (moveTo(), lineTo(), fillRect(), ...) that R's graphics engine generated while a plot was drawn.

Details

This package exists to answer the question "how does an R graphics device actually work?" by building one from scratch against R's public graphics device API (see R_ext/GraphicsDevice.h and R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h in the R source tree, or vignette("grDevices")-adjacent material). It is not meant to compete with mature canvas-based devices such as the archived canvas package or webr::canvas() – it deliberately keeps things simple (no raster image support, approximate text metrics, a single rectangular clip region at a time) so the source stays easy to read end to end.

The package's C source, in src/, is organised by responsibility:

  • device.c – the device lifecycle: creating it, closing it, starting new pages. This is the best starting point for understanding how a device registers itself with R.

  • draw.c – the drawing callbacks: lines, rectangles, circles, polygons, text, clipping.

  • colour.c – translating R's packed colour integers, line styles, and font descriptions into CSS/JS.

  • write.c – the HTML/JS text templates everything else writes into.

See cnvs() to open a device.
